title: South Texas builders take immigration workforce concerns to Washington
excerpt: South Texas business leaders met with U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar in Washington on Wednesday to raise concerns that immigration enforcement is worsening a construction worker shortage, delaying homebuilding and raising labor costs across the region.
content:
South Texas business leaders traveled to Washington to tell federal lawmakers that immigration enforcement is worsening a worker shortage in construction, delaying homebuilding and raising labor costs, according to KGNS.

The group met with U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar on Wednesday, Nov. 11. Laredo realtor Hector Alaniz said immigration raids were contributing to a shortage of workers that slows home construction, creating a domino effect of delays and higher labor costs, KGNS reported.

Benny Melendez of the South Texas Builders Association said workers, including some with legal papers, were afraid to show up to job sites. He also alleged that immigration authorities entered private properties without warrants and detained people before asking questions, according to KGNS.

Cuellar said strong border security can go together with respectful treatment of people, and he supported focusing enforcement on people with criminal records rather than those without them, KGNS reported. He said current enforcement is affecting the U.S. economy, construction and agriculture.

Melendez said he hopes the talks lead lawmakers to help construction workers obtain legal pathways to work permits, according to KGNS. The station said it had reached out to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement for comment and was awaiting a response.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 11, 2026.
